description: Candidate comparable parcels for a Texas unequal-appraisal comparison (Tax Code §41.43(b)(3)), from one tax year of the subject's appraisal district roll (the newest year whose roll gives the subject a value, or tax_year), with every field of the subject and the candidates read from that year's roll only: same county and tax year, the same state property category code, improvement area within area_band of the subject's, year built within year_band years when both are known; parcels sharing the subject's neighborhood code first (when the roll gives one), then its ZIP code, then the rest of the county if fewer than min_matches. Optional narrowing, off by default: same_building_class, same_local_use_code, local_use_codes. Each candidate and the subject carry their roll fields: id, apn (the district's account number), value and value_basis, value_per_sf (that value divided by the improvement area, to the cent: the roll's figures and one division, not an opinion of value), market and appraised value, improvement and land area, year built, state property category, local use code, neighborhood code, building class, situs address, tax year, and the citation of the value fact; the subject adds its value history by tax year. Separate land and improvement values are not returned. calc_args gives the same subject and candidates with exactly calc_tx_unequal_appraisal's input fields (tax_year, subject, comparables; id = the FactLot URN, label = the situs address, nulls left out, no adjustments): the candidate list under the default rule, not a selection by FactLot, for the caller to review and edit (remove, add or adjust comparables, each adjustment with a reason) before passing it to calc_tx_unequal_appraisal. Order of operations: registry_tx_equity_candidates, then the person's review, then calc_tx_unequal_appraisal with the reviewed calc_args, then report_create. selection echoes the rule, the effective parameters, the tax year and roll sources used, the files the compared values come from (compared_files: as-of date, and whether the file is dated before July 25 of the tax year, the certification date in Tax Code §26.01(a)), the subject's category, class, use code and area (subject_summary), each narrowing parameter and whether it was applied, how many parcels each step of the rule left (steps), the candidates counted by building class and by local use code with the subject's own beside them (class_counts, use_code_counts), and which tier each candidate came from; selection_rule restates the parameters used (tax year, category, area band and year band with their bounds, the subject summary, the narrowing applied, the step counts, counts per tier) with a notice that the list is the default rule's output (the default rule with the narrowing listed, when a narrowing was applied). Each candidate's citation.document_id names its entry in sources, which gives that snapshot's license, attribution, ai_use and redistribution: relay them with the candidate. Candidates under FactLot's default rule, a design choice, not a legal standard; a person decides which, if any, to use. For evidence calculations only: FactLot does not represent property owners, file protests, or advise whether to protest. Not an appraisal or an opinion of value (Tex. Occ. Code §1103.003(1)); not legal or tax advice and not a substitute for the advice of an attorney. Never returns owner names, mailing addresses, or ownership facts: ownership is outside this comparison and is not needed for it. Texas parcels only. Tarrant County is not served by the hosted registry while the publisher's terms for AI use are unclear. On the hosted API, a call without a Pro or Team key gets the current roll year only in the subject's value_history (the answer says so); the candidates are unchanged. Requires a FactLot Registry (public-record facts about commercial property, each cited to the source file and record).

apn.description: Appraisal district account number as the district prints it.

area_band.description: Improvement area band as a share of the subject's (0.35: within ±35%). Must be greater than 0.

county_fips.description: 3-digit Texas county FIPS, e.g. "201" for Harris County.

limit.description: Maximum candidates returned (1–200; a larger value is refused). Fewer are returned when fewer meet the rule, or when the neighborhood and ZIP code tiers hold at least min_matches, because the rest of the county is then not included; a warning gives the counts.

local_use_codes.description: Only parcels whose local use code is one of these, compared exactly as the roll prints them (1–50 codes). Default: no use-code test.

min_matches.description: Widen from the neighborhood and ZIP code tiers to the whole county when they hold fewer than this.

same_building_class.description: Only parcels whose building class (from the compared roll year) is exactly the subject's. Not applied, with a warning, when the subject has none. Default false: building class is not compared.

same_local_use_code.description: Only parcels whose local use code (the district's own use or class code) is exactly the subject's. Not applied, with a warning, when the subject has none or local_use_codes is given. Default false.

state_fips.description: With county_fips and apn: "48" (Texas), the only state served.

tax_year.description: Roll year to compare in: the subject and every candidate are read from that year's roll files only (building class also from that year's buildings file, named in selection.building_class_sources); selection.compared_files lists the files the compared values are cited from. Default: the newest tax year whose roll gives the subject a positive value. A year whose files hold values but no category code or improvement area gives no candidates, with a warning naming the missing facts. On the hosted API, tax_year needs a Pro or Team key.

urn.description: FactLot parcel URN of the subject, e.g. fl:parcel:us-48201:0011440000001. Give this, or county_fips and apn.

year_band.description: Year-built band in years, applied when both the subject's and the candidate's are known.

title: Texas unequal-appraisal candidates
